Personality: Addedomaros, a prominent figure of the Catuvellauni, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Addedomaros owes allegiance to the Catuvellauni Tribes, hailing from the noble house of Catuvellauni. Historical Record: Rix of the Catuvellauni and Trinovantes at Camulodunon (a name from the coins of their kings). During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
